# National Grid starts construction on Somerset substation supporting over 4,500 new jobs


- [Home](https://www.nationalgrid.com/)


18th November 2026


*Press release*


- Main construction has begun on National Grid’s new transmission substation near Woolavington, in Somerset
- The new substation will connect the Gravity Smart Campus to the electricity transmission network, including the Agratas battery manufacturing facility which will create 4,600 jobs and generate £700m in economic value for the South West
- A £530,000 fund will be available for local community projects


National Grid Electricity Transmission (NGET) has begun main construction of a new substation near Woolavington in Somerset which will support the creation of around 4,600 local jobs.


Once complete, the new 400kV substation will connect the Gravity Smart Campus to the electricity transmission network and provide the infrastructure needed to support growing electricity demand in the region.


The campus is home to the Agratas battery manufacturing facility, which will be one of Europe’s largest. It is expected to create around 4,600 direct jobs and generate over £700 million in economic value for the South West region each year once fully operational.


Woolavington forms part of National Grid’s £40 billion investment in its electricity networks over the next five years, supporting new industries and economic growth, and is also part of The Great Grid Upgrade, the largest upgrade of the transmission network in generations.


The main construction phase will include the installation of above-ground electrical infrastructure, steel structures and associated equipment. Three supergrid transformers are expected to be delivered to site in early 2027.


It comes after National Grid Electricity Distribution (NGED) built two interim 33kV connections to power the Agratas site until the high voltage 400kV substation is complete.


As part of the project, National Grid is establishing a £530,000 Community Fund to support projects that deliver lasting benefits for communities near to the new substation. The fund will be shaped through engagement with residents, charities, community groups and local representatives to ensure it reflects local priorities. Groups will be able to apply for funding from 2027.


**Cordi O'Hara OBE FEI, Executive President UK at National Grid, said:**


*“Starting main construction at Woolavington is an important milestone, not just for this project but for the growth it will help enable across the South West.*


*"By providing the electricity infrastructure needed by major new industrial developments like Gravity, we’re helping turn investment into jobs and long-term economic value.*


*“It’s a great example of the essential role the transmission network plays in supporting growth and meeting Britain’s changing electricity needs.”*


**Minister for Reindustrialisation Blair McDougall said:**


*"This is great news for Somerset and another big step towards powering the UK’s green industries of the future.*


*“Through our Modern Industrial Strategy we’re backing projects like Agratas’ with the investment they need to thrive, helping create thousands of skilled jobs for local communities.”*


**Brian Stonerock, Head of Capital Projects at Agratas, said:**


*"Access to a reliable power supply is essential for a facility of this scale, and this new infrastructure from National Grid will help provide the electricity needed to power our operations for years to come.*


*"We're building one of Europe's largest battery manufacturing facilities here in Somerset, creating around 4,600 jobs and supporting a new generation of skilled careers in manufacturing, engineering and technology. The new substation will help make that possible by providing the electricity needed to bring the site fully to life."*


**Tony Wilson, Managing Director of Balfour Beatty’s Power Transmission and Distribution business, said:**


*“We’re proud to be working with National Grid to deliver this important piece of infrastructure for Somerset and the wider South West.*


*“Reaching the start of main construction is an important milestone for the project. Drawing on our extensive experience in delivering complex energy infrastructure, we look forward to delivering the new substation, providing the resilient electricity network needed to support growing demand in the region.”*


Normal construction hours will be from 8am to 6pm Monday to Friday and 8am to 1pm on Saturdays. Some extended or weekend working may occasionally be required for equipment deliveries or specific construction activities. National Grid will coordinate these activities with Somerset Council and provide advance notice where work may affect nearby residents or businesses.


National Grid will continue to keep communities in Woolavington, Puriton and the surrounding area informed throughout construction through newsletters, postal updates and information published on the[project website](https://www.nationalgrid.com/electricity-transmission/network-and-infrastructure/infrastructure-projects/woolavington-substation#230548828-3170454567) .
